| Candidate | Count beside cup | Count / 28 |

<div class="glove-example-caption"><strong>Coffee wins:</strong> 12 of 28 observed neighbors. This answer comes directly from the counts.</div>

::: {.notes}
The final column is the empirical probability of a candidate token among this corpus's cup neighbors. The diagonal is zero because the corpus contains no repeated-token sentences. The five zero-count candidates tie; their order is arbitrary. These are unordered context associations and do not model sentence order.
:::

## Can short vectors reproduce those counts? {#glove-reconstruct-question .glove-example}

<div class="glove-reconstruct-target">Observed: <strong>coffee → cup = 12</strong></div>

| Learned parameter | Two coordinates | Bias |
|---|---|---:|
| coffee · word vector | `[0.547, -0.988]` | 0.777 |
| cup · context vector | `[0.564, -0.954]` | 0.449 |

$$\widehat{\ell}_{coffee,cup}=\mathbf w_{coffee}^T\widetilde{\mathbf w}_{cup}+b_{coffee}+\widetilde b_{cup}$$

<div class="glove-lookup-pause"><b>PAUSE</b><span>Multiply matching coordinates, add them, then add both biases. How close is the result to <strong>ln 12 ≈ 2.485</strong>?</span></div>

::: {.notes}
These are actual fitted parameters from a seeded two-dimensional GloVe model, not hand-picked coordinates. Both vector tables and bias tables were fitted against all nonzero cells in this exact matrix. The two-dimensional bottleneck shares parameters across cells. Training settings: seed 351; 400 AdaGrad epochs; learning rate 0.08; f(x) = min((x/10)^0.75, 1). Ten is a teaching setting for the weighting cap. Show the worked score on the next slide. Displayed parameters are rounded to three decimals.
:::

## Compare the predictions with the same data {#glove-reconstruction .glove-example}

| Pair | Count | Target: ln count | Before training | After training |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| coffee → cup | 12 | 2.485 | -0.004 | **2.477** |
| tea → cup | 10 | 2.303 | 0.001 | **2.323** |
| milk → cup | 4 | 1.386 | -0.007 | **1.311** |
| juice → cup | 2 | 0.693 | -0.001 | **0.751** |

<div class="glove-fit-score">coffee · cup + both biases ≈ <strong>2.477</strong><span>Target: 2.485</span></div>
<div class="glove-example-caption">Mean weighted squared error over all nonzero cells: <strong>3.571 → 0.0015</strong></div>
<div class="glove-example-question">What objective makes these predictions approach the log counts?</div>

::: {.notes}
The before/after entries are genuine outputs of the same model and matrix, at initialization and after training. The dot product plus biases predicts a log count, not a word probability. Zero cells are omitted from the GloVe loss, so they are not trained negative examples. Do not infer that zero-count pairs must receive low model scores. The loss is averaged over all positive directed cells, not just the four rows displayed here. Full values and settings are in glove-example-data.json; regenerate both the data and these slides with build_glove_example.py.
:::
